title.value: SAMPLE-EFFICIENT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING BY BREAKING THE REPLAY RATIO BARRIER
title.justification: The title reflects the main contribution of the paper, which focuses on improving reinforcement learning algorithms by enhancing the replay ratio scaling.
title.quote: S AMPLE -E FFICIENT R EINFORCEMENT L EARNING BY B REAKING THE R EPLAY R ATIO B ARRIER

extractions.description: The paper presents a technique for improving the sample efficiency of deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms by increasing the replay ratio during training. This involves resetting parameters of the RL agents to achieve better replay ratio scaling, leading to enhanced performance in established benchmarks like the Atari 100k and DeepMind Control Suite.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on enhancing reinforcement learning techniques rather than addressing climate or ecological sustainability issues. While it deals with efficient learning methods, it does not specifically relate these to sustainability goals such as climate change mitigation or adaptation.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we show that fully or partially resetting the parameters of deep reinforcement learning agents causes better replay ratio scaling capabilities to emerge.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes. It focuses on a methodological improvement in reinforcement learning without linking it to specific sustainability applications.
primary_category.quote: In many real world scenarios, each interaction with the environment comes at a cost, and it is desirable for deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to learn with a minimal amount of samples.

secondary_categories.justification: As the primary focus is on reinforcement learning efficiency, there are no direct secondary links to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
secondary_categories.quote: Despite generally providing limited benefit when applied to standard baselines (Fedus et al., 2020; Kumar et al., 2021), replay ratio scaling has been shown to bring performance improvements to well-tuned algorithms.

primary_sub_category.justification: Given that the paper does not relate directly to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, there is no applicable sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Both in continuous control, with SAC in DeepMind Control Suite (Haarnoja et al., 2018; Tassa et al., 2018), and discrete control, with SPR in Atari 100k (Schwarzer et al., 2021a; Kaiser et al., 2020), we break the replay ratio barrier, unlocking a training regime in which orders of magnitude of additional agent updates can be used to increase the performance.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no specific links to secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories as the focus remains technical within reinforcement learning.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The number of agent updates per environment step is usually called replay ratio, and most standard algorithms are trained with a value around 1.
